location: New York, NY (HQ) / San Francisco, CA / Remote (US) USA
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

As a member of Ramp's Risk Strategy & Operations, you will drive operational initiatives related to underwriting, customer risk management, and fraud. This role requires an understanding of underwriting processes, fluency with data, and the ability to analyze risk vectors such as credit and fraud risks. We take our responsibility to serve our customers’ commitment to their financial health seriously, and our approach is anchored in data-driven and systematic decisions to delight our customers.

Please note: This role follows a Sunday–Thursday workweek.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Develop and execute Ramp’s risk underwriting policy used to onboard new business to the Ramp platform across corporate credit card and bill pay products

 - Build and maintain monitoring dashboards for underwriting outcomes, processes and losses

 - Partner with product and engineering to build best in class risk tooling to increase operations efficiency

 - Research emerging underwriting and fraud trends to innovate on Ramp's decisioning systems and policies

 - Provide best in class customer experience, while managing credit and fraud risk, by effectively managing customer support requests on their application over phone and email

 - Have the ability to grow, develop and learn in a fast-paced, start-up environment

 - Identify emerging risks and use AI and automation to improve decision quality and efficiency




WHAT YOU NEED

 - Minimum 1-2 years of experience in Underwriting, Credit Risk Management or Fraud Risk Management

 - Experience within consumer/ corporate/ small business cards, payments, invoices, lending, or related industries

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills

 - Strong background in customer support via email

 - Investigative and critical thinking skills

 - BA/BS from an accredited university

 - Ability to work weekends from Sunday - Thursday

 - Experience integrating AI into your daily work




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience in high growth startups

 - Experience building complex financial products

 - Knowledge of SQL or Python

 - Strong background in customer support via phone

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
Who We Are 
 TrueComp partners with over 1,000 public sector agencies to modernize workforce planning, compensation, and benefits analysis. Its intuitive platform and expert consulting empower HR and finance leaders with transparency, efficiency, and equity to make smarter decisions in recruitment, retention, and budgeting. TrueComp provides instant and actionable insights to help government organizations attract top talent, optimize labor strategies, and achieve long-term fiscal sustainability. Dedicated to simplifying workforce challenges, TrueComp ’s solutions enable data-driven decisions that improve organizational performance and drive meaningful outcomes. TrueComp was recognized among the Top 100 Government Services companies on the 2024 Inc. 5000.
 About the role 
 The Customer Success Manager owns a book of 50-75 public agency accounts from the point a customer has produced real work in the platform through renewal. They are accountable for retention and adoption across that book.
 Our customers are HR directors, finance directors, and the analysts who support them. They use TrueComp to price union proposals, build salary schedules, and defend numbers in front of elected officials. Success in this role depends on being credible in those conversations, not just responsive to them.
 Roughly 15-20 accounts are named accounts managed on a set cadence. The remainder are covered through scheduled check-ins and usage-based triggers. Every account renews annually and the Customer Success Manager owns that conversation start to finish.
 This role reports to the Chief Operations Officer and works closely with sales, support, and product.
 What you'll do 
 Retention and Renewal 
 Own the renewal conversation for every account in your book, from early positioning through signed agreement.
 Run a renewal calendar that starts 120 days out, not 30. In public sector, the paperwork takes longer than the decision.
 Negotiate pricing and terms within your approved authority, and bring anything outside that band to the COO with a recommendation.
 Manage the mechanics — purchase orders, fiscal year timing, contract amendments, and re-bid requirements where they apply.
 Forecast renewals accurately and identify risk early enough to change the outcome.
 Maintain an account health view you can defend in a forecast review.
 Customer Relationships 
 Build working relationships with HR and finance leadership at each agency, not just your day-to-day contact.
 Understand each customer's operating calendar — budget adoption, bargaining cycles, council meetings — and plan engagement around it.
 Run a consistent cadence with named accounts covering usage, upcoming budget and negotiation cycles, and open issues.
 Own escalations end to end, pulling in support, product, or executive help when the situation calls for it.
 Identify and qualify expansion opportunities across additional modules, added agencies, and consulting engagements, and hand them to sales with the context needed to run them.
 Collaboration and Product Input 
 Route customer feedback and feature requests into the roadmap process with enough context and evidence for product and engineering to act.
 Work alongside the Onboarding Specialist from kickoff forward so the transition to your ownership is a handoff, not a reintroduction.
 Share patterns you see across your book with the broader team — recurring friction, competitive pressure, emerging use cases.
 Process and Tools 
 Track account activity, renewal forecasts, and escalations in Salesforce and keep records current.
 Contribute to building the customer success playbook. We are a 30-person company and you will help define process, not just follow it.
 Qualifications 
 Direct experience inside or alongside public sector HR or finance. That may be working at an agency, or working with agency HR and finance teams in a vendor, consulting, or advisory capacity.
 Working knowledge of compensation benchmarking, labor costing, or actuarial analysis. You do not need to be an actuary. You do need to hold your own in a conversation with a compensation analyst.
 Direct ownership of renewal outcomes in a prior role, including pricing conversations and negotiation.
 Working knowledge of public sector procurement — purchase orders, fiscal year cycles, contract amendments, and when a renewal becomes a competitive re-bid.
 3-5 years managing customer relationships with direct retention and renewal accountability. SaaS experience preferred, not required.
 Demonstrated ability to manage a book of this size independently, prioritizing across accounts without close supervision.
 Written communication clear and concise enough that an HR director will actually read it.
 Preferred: Salesforce experience, prior work at a company under 100 employees, data literacy strong enough to read a usage report and know what it means.

About Us: 
 At Reusables, we’re driven by a vision of a waste-free world and recognize the urgent need to address the environmental impact of our current systems and habits. We believe that meaningful change requires institutions to offer frictionless systems that make sustainability effortless and tangible. 
 What began as a grassroots initiative offering reusable takeout containers to restaurants and cafes in Vancouver, has since grown into an enterprise technology platform reaching institutions across North America. Today, Reusables is helping to eliminate thousands of tonnes of single-use waste each year, empowering businesses to join the journey toward a cleaner, more sustainable future. 
 As a venture-backed and mission-driven company, we are passionate about making impact at scale. We are a young, weirdly talented group of ‘high-octane’ individuals that are relentlessly focused on the planet, people, and profit – in that order. 
 About the Role: 
 You’ll own the client relationship from contract signature through to renewal. You’re the connective tissue between our clients and every internal team: the person who keeps everyone accountable to the onboarding checklist, communicates with confidence when things go sideways, and knows your accounts well enough to spot an opportunity before the client does. 
 Your contribution is client satisfaction, retention and expansion: making sure clients get real value from Reusables, watching for the signals that point to churn, and finding the opportunities to grow each account. 
 You’ll sit in our Client Delivery team, which gets clients live and keeps them successful. 
 Most of our clients are universities, so the year follows the academic calendar: launches cluster ahead of each fall semester, and most renewals follow the end of the academic year.  This is a full-time, permanent, remote position, open to candidates anywhere in the United States. The working hours for this role will be EST or CST.

 November to February: Regular check-ins, account health reviews and the smaller off-cycle renewals 
 March to April: End-of-semester reviews, some launches, and renewal and expansion work for the next academic year 
 What You’ll Bring To The Team: 
 Account management or customer success experience with B2B clients, from onboarding through renewal

title: Senior Client Engagement Manager (Post-Pay)
description:

 Requirements Ownership and Artifact Governance

You will run several onboardings at once, each with its own timeline, stakeholders, and configuration requirements, and keep every one of them moving. The value of this role is improving time to value for every new customer while giving them an excellent onboarding experience and making sure they achieve the outcomes they came to Cofactr for. You will get customers from signed contract to configured, enabled, and placing orders faster, without cutting corners on the setup or the relationship.
 You are the coordinator between Sales, Customer Success, and the customer. You review what Sales captured in discovery, close the gaps before configuration starts, drive account setup to completion, and line up the enablement sessions our CSMs lead. Your work lets CSMs spend their time on enablement and account growth instead of logistics, and it gets customers to their first purchase (major value milestone) faster. This role requires operational rigor , a project management mindset , strong communication skills , cross functional relationship building , and the discipline to track many concurrent projects without letting one stall.

 Sales-to-CS Handoff: Own the handoff for every new customer. Review the configuration discovery and intake materials from Sales, identify missing requirements, and resolve open questions with Sales and the customer before work begins. Close the knowledge gap. 
 Onboarding Project Management: Run each onboarding as a project with a defined plan, milestones, owners, and target dates. Track status across all active onboardings and flag risks early.

 Enablement Coordination: Schedule and prepare CSM-led enablement sessions and office hours, including attendees, agendas, and customer pre-work, so the CSM can focus on delivering the session and the customer arrives ready.

 Process Improvement: Work with CS leadership to refine onboarding playbooks, intake forms, checklists, and templates as volume grows.
 Metrics and Reporting: Track onboarding metrics such as time from close to configuration complete, time to first enablement session, time to first purchase, and number of onboardings in flight, and use them to find and remove delays.
 What We're Looking For
 Experience: 4+ years in customer onboarding, implementation, or project management in a B2B SaaS or technology environment.
 Extra credit for supply chain, procurement, or hardware/manufacturing industry experience
 Extreme Ownership: You treat every onboarding as your own from handoff to enablement, and when something stalls, you find the blocker, pull in the right people, and see it through to resolution.
 Concurrent Project Management: A track record of running multiple customer projects at once, each with its own timeline, stakeholders, and milestones.
 Organization and Follow-Through: You keep a clean tracker, run tight meetings, and close loops without being reminded.
 Communication: Clear written and verbal communication with customers and internal teams, including the ability to push for decisions and hold stakeholders to dates.
 Technical Aptitude: Comfortable learning and configuring SaaS platforms, and able to diagnose a setup issue well enough to route it to the right person.
 Tech Stack Experience: Familiarity with tools like SFDC, Pylon, Notion, Gainsight, or Metabase; ability to quickly learn new platforms.
 AI Literacy: Hands-on experience using AI tools such as Claude in your daily work, for example to draft customer communications, summarize calls, build trackers, or automate repetitive steps, and the curiosity to find new ways to apply them to onboarding.
 Adaptability: Comfortable in an early-stage environment where processes are still being built.
 Why Join Us
 High Impact: You will own the onboarding experience for every new Cofactr customer, the first impression that sets up their success on the platform.

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
About Us
 STACK is a leading provider of cloud-based construction software solutions, committed to helping businesses transform their workflows from first bid through final handoff. We pride ourselves on fostering a collaborative, dynamic environment where team members have the opportunity to grow and make a real impact.
 About the Role:
 Contractors buy STACK to change how they bid and build. Your job is to make sure that happens. As a Customer Success Manager , you'll own a book of about 440 growing contractor teams – companies with two to four STACK users – and help each of them get real, lasting value from the platform.
 You'll work from customer signals. When usage drops, a renewal gets close, or a new user goes quiet, you'll know about it and reach out with a plan. It's a great fit for someone who cares about customer outcomes and wants their time to go where it makes the biggest difference.
 What You’ll Do:
 Own a named book of about 440 accounts. Keep a current health score on every account, refresh it monthly, and know where each customer is in their journey.
 Respond to customer signals within 48 hours. Each signal points to one account and one specific problem. Pick the right play, act on it, and record the result so the team learns what works. When an account goes quiet, treat that as a signal too.
 Drive adoption and value. Our north star is customers doing real work: someone active in STACK on at least five days in the last 30. Find the accounts that have slipped and help them get back on track with practical, workflow-focused conversations.
 Manage renewals. Keep a renewal calendar for your book and start every renewal conversation at least 90 days out. Automated reminders handle the routine work, so you can focus on results.
 Protect and grow seats. Help customers keep the users they have and add more as their teams grow. Spot expansion opportunities and pass qualified leads to our sales team.
 Forecast accurately. Call commit, risk, and lost renewals by name each week.
 Be your customers' go-to contact. Answer workflow questions yourself, bring in Support for product issues, and loop in our Industry Consultants for trade-specific work.
 Pick up accounts from implementation. Accounts with two or more users join your book from our Onboarding & Consulting team at day 120.
 Onboarding and Time to First Value:
 The first 90 days shape the whole customer relationship. Our Onboarding & Consulting team gets new customers to first value. You step in when the signals show a customer is stuck, and you help that early momentum last.
 First value is a completed takeoff in week one. Customers who run a takeoff in their first week are 4.72x more likely to still be active at day 30. Every new user added to an account should reach that same milestone.
 Work closely with Onboarding & Consulting. Know which incoming accounts missed early milestones before they reach your book, so nothing gets lost in the handoff.
 Share what you learn. You'll often spot a pattern before the data does. Bring it to Onboarding & Consulting and Digital Success so the whole program gets better.
 How Success Is Measured:
 We measure you on the work you can influence day to day. Company-wide results like gross and net revenue retention matter too, and the whole team shares them. 
 Primary measure: Percentage of your book with a current health score, refreshed monthly
 Secondary measures: Signals answered within 48 hours, signal queue cleared daily, renewals started 90 days out, forecast accuracy each quarter
 Team goals: Customers doing real work across the enterprise segment, week-one takeoff rate, month-three usage rate, net seat retention rate, gross revenue retention
 Your First 90 Days:
 Weeks 1–3: Get to know your book and set a health score on every account. Start working renewal and usage-risk alerts right away.
 Weeks 2–6: Build a renewal calendar for the next four quarters, and start any renewal that's already inside the 90-day window.
 Weeks 4–8: Focus on accounts at risk of reducing seats, and reach out to customers who have stopped using STACK.
 Weeks 8–12: Run your first full forecast cycle and compare it with actual results at quarter end.
 What You Bring:
 4+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a similar customer-facing role in B2B SaaS, including at least 2 years owning enterprise or strategic accounts. 
 Experience managing a named book of hundreds of accounts, with a realistic approach to how you spend your time.
 A habit of acting on what customers are doing in the product, and the discipline to keep your queue clear.
 Comfort holding a renewal conversation and a workflow conversation in the same call, with customer value leading the way.
 Curiosity about the product. You'll use STACK yourself so you can help customers solve real problems.
 A careful, accurate approach to forecasting.
 An understanding of seat growth as a retention strategy. Customers with more than one user are far more likely to stay.
 Experience in construction or estimating is a plus. Familiarity with Salesforce and Gong is expected.
 What We're Building:
 Our Customer Experience team is building a signal engine that brings risk, adoption, and expansion signals together in one place. Today, much of that work happens by hand with renewal tracking and usage alerts in Slack. Over the next two quarters, we're adding nightly risk monitoring, a single work queue, and automated digital outreach, followed by recommended plays for each signal. You'll help shape how it works.
 How Our Team Works:
 Five beliefs guide how our Customer Experience team serves customers:
 Meet customers where they are. A one-person roofing company and a 40-person general contractor get the same commitment, delivered in the way that fits each of them best.
 No customer left behind. Every customer gets our full activation program, including in-app guidance, learning paths, community, and webinars.
